newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danisco sees 10-12 pct growth in full year.
newsitem.headline: Danisco sees 10-12 pct growth in full year.

text.p: Danish packaging, foods, drinks and sugar group Danisco A/S posted on Wednesday eight percent higher first-half 1996/97 profits and forecast that the whole year result would fall within its 10-12 percent annual profit growth target.

"As announced previously Danisco has set itself a long-term target to improve results by between 10-12 percent annually. Our expectations for whole year 1996/97 are the same," Danisco said in a statement accompanying its interim result.
Danisco posted a first-half 1996/97 pre-tax and extraordinary items profit of 851 million crowns.
This compared with 785 million crowns in the same period last year. Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast an average 844 million crown ordinary pre-tax result for the period.
Turnover was up six percent at 8.319 billion crowns, Danisco said, despite difficult conditions for its packaging division with lower prices due to stiffer competition.

Otherwise Food and Beverages advanced with sales of Danish schnapps increased despite new duties in the home market and its Ingredients sector managed to up turnover by 11 percent, noting solid gains in eastern Europe, central and south America and southeast Asia.

Danisco, Europe's fourth biggest sugar producer, with factories in Denmark, Sweden and Germany, forecast its total sugar production for 1996 would be around one million tonnes, up on its EU quota of 921,000 and 1995's 922,000 overall output.
The Danisco share was only affected minimally by the result, rising two crowns to 337 by 1300 gmt. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
